question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,dx]\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[\operatorname{sin}⁡x]_{0}^{y}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡0)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy & =[-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)-(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)\end{aligned}
$$
